subject: Redwood - Procurement & Security Qualification for Acme (PO vs Marketplace)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Barnes <kelly.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood - Procurement & Security Qualification for Acme (post-call recap)

Hi Kelly 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so were all aligned and to capture next steps: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: Proof-of-concept for Acmes internal assistant (customer support triage) with predictable latency and cost.
- Expected initial footprint: ~5k monthly active users, ~200M tokens/month expected as we ramp.
- Key procurement question: do you prefer POs (standard for Acme) or will you use corporate card for initial POC purchases? Also asked if Acme prefers marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace/GCP Marketplace).
- Security gating: Acme needs SOC 2 Type II summary, a standard DPA, and answers to our security questionnaire before procurement can proceed.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether Procurement requires a PO and P-card is not acceptable for pilot? That will determine our billing path and SOW cadence.
2) If PO: can you share your standard PO timeline (days to issue) and any required contract redline point people?
3) Oliver (IT Security)  well share SOC 2 summary & our standard DPA. Are there any additional artifacts you need (pen test, network diagram, encryption details)?
4) Dev on our side will help with any technical questions on integration and enterprise deployment options (VPC/private).

Ill attach the SOC 2 summary and our standard DPA in my next email (sending both as stubs to speed your review). Also linking our security questionnaire for Oliver to review  its a short prefilling to speed the audit.

Proposed timeline: If we can confirm PO vs card and receive feedback on the DPA by next Wed (3/18), we can target a POC start the week of 3/23.

Thanks  Ill follow up with the documents.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: (will send in follow-up)

From: Kelly Barnes <kelly.barnes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood - Procurement & Security Qualification for Acme (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa  appreciate the clear summary. A few quick answers from Procurement side: 

- PO vs Card: For pilots under $25k we can usually use a corporate card, but anything that needs an annual commitment or vendor terms generally goes via PO. For your pricing/commit ask, we expect procurement to prefer PO for anything recurring.
- Marketplace: We prefer AWS Marketplace when available because it simplifies billing and cost allocation tags. If Redwood is on marketplace and the SKU matches our expected spend, Procurement will likely go that route.
- Timeline: Typical PO issuance is 710 business days after we have an executed DPA/contract signature and approved SOW.

Security: Oliver  we need SOC 2 Type II summary + DPA to start formal review. If you can provide those this week, well kick off the security questionnaire. Also confirm whether your DPA supports standard Acme addenda (data residency & subprocessor list).

Tagging the security folks: Oliver, what else do you need from Redwood to begin internal review?

Best,
Kelly Barnes
Senior Procurement Partner | Acme Corporation
kelly.barnes@acme.com
